R306.note: filepath.IsLocal rejects absolute/.. entry names, correctly closing Zip Slip; preserves extraction of legitimate relative entries (symlink claim in the explanation is inaccurate but not a functional defect).

R307.note: Saved extension is now derived from the validated MIME allowlist instead of the attacker-controlled originalname, so a dangerous extension can no longer be saved regardless of spoofed MIME; legitimate png/jpeg uploads unaffected.

R308.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching every sibling admin route; correctly closes the missing-authorization gap with no unrelated behavior change.

R309.note: Allowlist mapping is the right pattern for a dynamic require sink, but the write-up itself admits the two-entry list ('reporting', 'analytics') is a placeholder standing in for the real plugin set, so as shipped it could reject legitimate plugin names not in that list.

R310.note: Ownership-scoped DELETE query is correct, but both the new interceptor and the handler gate on ctx.Value("user_id") which nothing in the shown code ever populates from incoming request metadata - an unstated assumption that, if wrong, denies every legitimate caller too.

R311.note: Switches to proper RESP array/bulk-string framing, the correct fix for a raw Redis socket; also incidentally fixes a pre-existing bug where notes containing spaces would have corrupted the old inline command.

R312.note: Loop bound changed from i<=n to i<n, exactly matching the stated contract (copy n events, no more).

R313.note: offset>capacity / length>capacity-offset checks (in that order, avoiding underflow) exactly match the stated contract: valid nonzero-offset writes still work, oversized writes are rejected, capacity still passed explicitly.

R314.note: Ownership check correctly added, but returns Forbid() (403) for an existing invoice owned by someone else, distinguishable from NotFound() (404) - the contract explicitly requires unauthorized IDs not reveal more than the not-found path, and this reveals the invoice's existence.

R315.note: Unix branch (/bin/ls with array args) is properly fixed, but the Windows branch still invokes cmd.exe /c directly with attacker-controlled data as a separate ProcessBuilder arg - cmd.exe re-parses the reassembled command line for &, |, etc. regardless of Java's array-based quoting, the same cmd.exe re-entry gap called out in the R320 case in this same batch.

R316.note: Table-name allowlist is the only viable fix since identifiers can't be parameterized; matches the stated contract that the default table still works and alternates are chosen only via server-owned mapping, not raw request text.

R317.note: Drops the shell entirely (direct exec.Command of the traceroute binary with an argument array plus a -- terminator) and adds hostname/IP format validation that doesn't reject any legitimate traceroute target.

R318.note: jwt.decode() replaced with jwt.verify() plus a hardcoded algorithms list, correctly requiring a valid signature; no behavior change for callers holding genuinely signed tokens.

R319.note: new Function() replaced with mathjs compile/evaluate, a purpose-built sandboxed expression evaluator; supports the required order.total + order.tax member-access arithmetic while rejecting calls like require()/process that aren't valid mathjs syntax.

R320.note: System.setProperty("jdk.lang.Process.allowAmbiguousCommands",...) is set inside the per-request handler, but this JDK security property is read once into a cached static field at ProcessImpl class-init, almost certainly already loaded before this call in a running server, making the set a no-op; even if it took effect, it hardens Java's own argv quoting, not cmd.exe's own &,| command chaining once it re-parses the .bat invocation, so CWE-78 remains open for this sink.
